a.summary: The rewritten createInstruction doc says diagnostic toString() zero-pads past the array end, but for offset < 0 or offset > data.length with len > 0 it throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException — the same spans the new hashCode guard refuses to read.
a.failure_scenario: `Instruction.createInstruction(programId, List.of(), new byte[]{1,2,3}, 4, 1).toString()` throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: arraycopy: length -1 is negative` instead of rendering zero-padded data. Same for a negative offset: `(new byte[]{1,2,3}, -1, 1).toString()` throws `arraycopy: source index -1 out of bounds for byte[3]`, and `(new byte[]{1,2,3}, Integer.MAX_VALUE, 1).toString()` throws too. A caller who took the doc at its word and logged an instruction inside a catch block or an error path loses the log line to a second exception.

b.summary: The corrected `toString` doc stops one case short: for a positive length `Arrays.copyOfRange` zero-pads only when `offset` is within the array; a larger or negative `offset` makes the diagnostic `toString()` throw, and an `offset + len` overflow makes it `OutOfMemoryError`. Neither case is documented or pinned.
b.failure_scenario: `Instruction.createInstruction(PROGRAM, List.of(), new byte[]{1}, 5, 2).toString()` -> `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: arraycopy: length -4 is negative`, so a log statement or debugger inspection kills the caller. `Instruction.createInstruction(PROGRAM, List.of(), new byte[]{1}, -1, 1).toString()` -> `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: arraycopy: source index -1 out of bounds for byte[1]`. Worst of the three, `Instruction.createInstruction(PROGRAM, List.of(), new byte[]{1}, 1, Integer.MAX_VALUE).toString()` — the exact fixture the new hash test constructs at InstructionBuildingTests.java:316 — wraps `offset + len` to `Integer.MIN_VALUE`, so `copyOfRange` computes `newLength == Integer.MAX_VALUE` and raises `OutOfMemoryError: Requested array size exceeds VM limit`.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
